name: Extragonadal Non-Dysgerminomatous Germ Cell Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Germ Cell Tumors

criteria.description: Tumor located outside the gonads (mediastinum, retroperitoneum, pineal gland, or sacrococcygeal region)
Histological confirmation of non-dysgerminomatous germ cell tumor subtype (e.g., embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, choriocarcinoma, teratoma)
Elevated serum tumor markers such as alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and/or beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of an extragonadal tumor with histopathological confirmation of non-dysgerminomatous germ cell tumor subtype; serum tumor markers supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of primary gonadal tumor by imaging or surgical exploration is essential to confirm extragonadal origin.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mediastinal mass with superior vena cava syndrome
pathognomonic.notes: Common in mediastinal extragonadal tumors causing vascular compression
searchTerms: upper chest tumor with vein swelling
mediastinal tumor causing blood flow obstruction

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of yolk sac tumor components
Associated with choriocarcinoma or embryonal carcinoma elements

common.notes: Compression of airways or lung tissue
searchTerms: shortness of breath due to mass effect
dyspnea caused by tumor pressing on lungs
pain in belly or lower back
unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

occasional.notes: Due to β-hCG secretion causing hormonal imbalance

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms from pineal region tumors
searchTerms: neurological problems due to pineal mass
vision and movement issues from brain tumor
discomfort in scrotum with no mass

rare.symptomName: Superior vena cava syndrome with facial edema
searchTerms: superior vena cava syndrome with facial puffiness
upper body swelling and vein obstruction

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to pineal tumor obstruction
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain fluid accumulation due to tumor
balance and movement problems from immune reaction

imaging: CT or MRI showing extragonadal mass in mediastinum, retroperitoneum, or pineal region
PET scan demonstrating metabolic activity of tumor
Ultrasound to exclude primary gonadal tumor
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic alterations may include isochromosome 12p
other: Histopathological confirmation via biopsy showing non-dysgerminomatous germ cell tumor components

distinguishingFeatures: Tumor localized to testes or ovaries
Lack of elevated AFP or β-hCG
Thymic origin confirmed by imaging and histology
No elevated germ cell tumor markers

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mediastinal or retroperitoneal mass
Severe respiratory distress or superior vena cava syndrome
Markedly elevated AFP or β-hCG indicating aggressive tumor
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Urinary System and Male Genital Organs, 2016
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Testicular Cancer, Version 2.2024
Orphanet: Extragonadal Non-Dysgerminomatous Germ Cell Tumor (ORPHA:99913)
